title: CIDI 3.0 Bipolar Screening Scale
instructions: Administer the two stem questions first. If either stem is endorsed, administer the Criterion B gate; if the gate is endorsed, count the 9 symptom items.

score.missing_response_policy: stem and gate questions determine whether the symptom-count risk table should be interpreted

items.text: Restlessness or agitation (pacing, inability to sit still)
Decreased need for sleep (4 hours or less without fatigue)

severity_bands.label: Very Low Risk
severity_bands.action: Low CIDI symptom count; interpret in clinical context and continue differential assessment as indicated

severity_bands.label: Low Risk
severity_bands.action: Consider comprehensive bipolar assessment if history, course, family history, or antidepressant activation raises concern

severity_bands.label: Moderate Risk
severity_bands.action: Recommend comprehensive psychiatric evaluation for bipolar spectrum disorder and differential diagnoses

severity_bands.label: High Risk
severity_bands.action: Recommend prompt psychiatric evaluation; assess safety, episode history, substance/medical contributors, and treatment implications

severity_bands.label: Very High Risk
severity_bands.action: High probability screen; arrange urgent comprehensive psychiatric evaluation and safety assessment

report.heading: CIDI 3.0 Bipolar Screening Scale
report.scoring_note: Scoring: after a positive stem and Criterion B gate, count the 9 symptom questions endorsed yes and map the 0-9 count to the risk table.
report.screening_note: The CIDI bipolar screen estimates risk and does not establish a bipolar diagnosis. Positive screens require clinical interview, longitudinal course review, substance/medical differential, and safety assessment.
